# Capture cards

<!-- Generated by tools/capture-cards-table from capture-cards/*.md; edit those. -->

Which capture cards protoHDMIcapture has seen, by USB id. Cheap cards share
a handful of chips, often under borrowed USB ids, so each chip has one
profile in [`capture-cards/`](../capture-cards/) listing the ids it appears
under and what is known about them. The setup wizard reads the same files.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Tested** | A real source played end to end here: picture, audio and sync. |
| **Probed** | Plugged in and its modes and frame rates measured; no source played yet. |
| **Reported** | Known only from vendor docs or third parties; never in our hands. |

| Chip | USB id | Link | Best mode | Status | Date | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MacroSilicon MS2109](../capture-cards/ms2109.md) | `534d:2109` | 480 Mbit/s | MJPEG 1280x720 @ 60 | Probed | 2026-10-13 | no source yet; modes and frame rates measured |
| [MacroSilicon MS2130](../capture-cards/ms2130.md) | `1e4e:7016` | 5000 Mbit/s | YUYV 1920x1080 @ 60 | Tested | 2026-09-06 | PS5: picture, audio and sync at YUYV 1080p60 |
| [MacroSilicon MS2130](../capture-cards/ms2130.md) | `345f:2130` | 5000 Mbit/s | YUYV 1920x1080 @ 60 | Reported |  | common id for MS2130 boards |
| [MacroSilicon MS2130](../capture-cards/ms2130.md) | `534d:2130` | 5000 Mbit/s | YUYV 1920x1080 @ 60 | Reported |  | MacroSilicon's own vendor id |

## Adding a card

1. Run `./view.sh --setup` with the card plugged into the port you will use.
   It prints the USB id, the link speed and the modes, and writes a
   Markdown report to `~/.local/state/protohdmicapture/`.
2. If the id is in a profile, add a `Status:` line for it there; otherwise
   add the id to the chip's profile, or start a new one by copying an
   existing file.
3. Run `tools/capture-cards-table` to regenerate this page.

## Profile shape

One Markdown file per chip, `capture-cards/<chip>.md`:

- `# <maker> <chip>` on the first line.
- `Ids:` every USB id seen for the chip; `Vendors:` vendor ids that make an
  unknown id "this maker's family".
- `Link:` the fastest link the chip uses (480 or 5000 Mbit/s), so a USB 2
  chip on USB 2 is not flagged.
- `Best:` the best mode it captures; `Hint:` one line the wizard shows.
- `Status: <id> <tested|probed|reported> <YYYY-MM-DD or -> <note>`, one per id.
- `## Quirks`: bullets; `[vid:pid]` at the start ties one to that id.
- `## References`: links to the sources the profile rests on.
